overall: This is defensibly LOD-300-partout, not 400 — and one system short of even that: plumbing sits at 250 because two of its three 300 criteria (dataset pipe sizes, rough-in heights) have zero test coverage and the 3-inch main drain member can never be emitted. Everything that exists is unusually well built: 216 passing tests with real numeric geometry assertions (three.js Euler endpoint reconstruction, hand-tallied CMU counts, NEC property tests over 400 random walls), a passing sub-50ms perf gate at LOD 400 all-systems, honest ASSUMPTION/LOD-400 comments, and instanced rendering that keeps draw calls at ~4 buckets. But not a single system reaches 350: there are no corner assemblies or partition backing, no joist hangers or stairwell framing, no jack rafters (and four roof types emit nothing), no footing corner continuity or rebar, no circuits, no Manhattan MEP routing, no drain slope, and the takeoff is a flat list with no per-system sections, sheet counts, cut lists, or fastener schedules. Next round I would attack: (1) the plumbing test debt and dead main-drain path, (2) hip end planes and the unframed roof types, (3) corner conditions everywhere (wall corners double-place end studs, CMU corners double-stack — 9 overlapping block pairs verified, footings stop dead at corners), and (4) the panel's truncated takeoff, which currently hides the one flag a builder must not miss.
